clue.text: She wants to play a part

definitions.text: She wants to play a part

parts.words: She wants to play a part
parts.note: a woman who hopes to be cast in a stage or screen role

explanation.surface: Someone longs to join in and contribute.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'play a part' as joining in, it sounds general; taken literally it is theatrical casting, and 'She' makes the performer female.
explanation.definitionFit: A female performer is someone who seeks roles in plays and films.

clue.text: Tempt pop back to ring the bells

indicators.note: back says the word for pop is read from right to left

parts.note: pop is a familiar word for father, PA
a peal is a ringing of church bells, used as a verb here

explanation.surface: Encouraging father to go back and toll the church bells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' looks like a verb but is a familiar name for a father, and 'back' turns only that piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt someone is to attract or allure them, as something with appeal does.

clue.text: Hearing about bishop of clannish nature

indicators.note: about means the trial word goes around the letter for bishop

parts.note: a court hearing is a trial
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A court case involving a cleric with a sectarian streak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places B inside TRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Clannish behaviour is loyalty to one's own group or tribe.

clue.text: English humanists displayed fervour

indicators.note: displayed suggests the letters of humanists are laid out afresh in another order

explanation.surface: English thinkers of the humanist school showed passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed' looks like a verb in the surface's past tense but signals a rearrangement of the second word only.
explanation.definitionFit: Fervour is intense eager passion, a close synonym.

clue.text: Sounds like Sean was fleeced

indicators.note: Sounds like tells us the name is to be heard, not read, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: the Irish name Sean is pronounced like Shawn

explanation.surface: Apparently a man named Sean was swindled.
explanation.walkthrough: In British (non-rhotic) speech the name and the past participle of shear sound alike. 'Fleeced' looks like cheated but means relieved of a fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheep that has had its wool clipped off has been sheared.

clue.text: Come to grips as king George takes fruit

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George, as on British postboxes
an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: A monarch wrestles as he seizes some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: GR is the royal cipher of King George (Georgius Rex), seen on British postboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to grips with an opponent is to wrestle or tackle them.

clue.text: Late destination for sombre detectives

parts.note: sombre means serious or grave
the Yard is Scotland Yard, London's Metropolitan Police detectives

explanation.surface: Gloomy police officers heading somewhere at the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' means dead, not tardy: where the deceased finally go. The Yard is Scotland Yard, London police headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cemetery is where the deceased are finally laid to rest.

clue.text: Feature in commercial when retired

indicators.note: in places the verb for feature inside the advert word

parts.note: a commercial is an advert, AD
to feature in something is to be present there, so the verb be

explanation.surface: Appearing in a television advert after giving up work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' means gone to bed, not stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has turned in for the night is lying in bed.

clue.text: Mollified at being included in set

indicators.note: being included in puts the little word at inside the word for set

parts.note: to set something down is to place it, so placed

explanation.surface: Calmed down after being put in a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' is the past participle, placed, and 'being included in' makes the two-letter word sit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mollified has been soothed and appeased.

clue.text: See cockney macho types by appointment? Correct!

indicators.note: a cockney speaker drops the H sound at the start of words

parts.note: he-men are macho types
a date is an appointment

explanation.surface: Look at tough East End men with a booking: right?
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney (East London) speech drops initial H, so he-men become 'EMEN; 'See' and 'by' just lead in.
explanation.definitionFit: To emendate a text is to amend it, putting errors right.

clue.text: Penny isn't to produce artwork

parts.note: ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A woman named Penny is not inclined to create art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a name but is the coin abbreviation P.
explanation.definitionFit: To paint is to create a picture with brush and colour.

clue.text: Usually about to reveal one's birthday

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject
to aver is to declare openly
a birthday marks the number of years one has lived

explanation.surface: Typically thinking of disclosing one's date of birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link here; each birthday adds a year to one's age.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true as a rule holds generally, typically, in most cases.

clue.text: Trouble ensues after a chap employs copyists

indicators.note: after puts the troubled letters of ensues behind a and chap

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: trouble as a verb means to stir up, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: Problems follow when a man takes on scribes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' looks like a noun in the surface but works as a verb, stirring up the letters of 'ensues', which come 'after' the first two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An amanuensis is a secretary who writes from dictation or copies manuscripts.

clue.text: Alleged to be unhappy when I intervened

indicators.note: intervened means the letter I comes between the letters of the word for unhappy

parts.note: unhappy means sad

explanation.surface: Supposedly miserable when I stepped in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intervened' puts I into SAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alleged has been stated or claimed.

clue.text: Serious complaint from lily-livered seaman

parts.note: lily-livered means cowardly, yellow
a jack or jack tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A grave grievance from a cowardly sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' is an illness, not a grievance: yellow jack is yellow fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow jack is an old name for yellow fever, a serious tropical illness.

clue.text: Test items man manufactured? That's a lie

indicators.note: manufactured suggests the letters of the three words are made into something new

explanation.surface: A man made test pieces, but the claim is false.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufactured' rearranges TEST ITEMS MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A false statement is an untruth, which a lie is.

clue.text: Permitting the existence of pain

definitions.meaning: to suffer something is to tolerate or allow it

explanation.definitionFit: Allowing or tolerating something is an old sense; enduring agony or distress is the common one.

clue.text: Not on watch, so taken unawares

explanation.definitionFit: Off duty as a sentry; caught by surprise while unprepared.

clue.text: Stop before I get on horse

indicators.note: before puts the word for stop in front of the other pieces

parts.note: to stall is to stop

explanation.surface: Halt before I mount the horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get' is a link; the pieces are simply run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A stallion is an uncastrated male horse.

clue.text: Very well! Turn it into a violin!

definitions.meaning: humorously, to adapt something to suit a fiddle

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in perfect health; read literally, it is adapting something to suit a fiddle.

clue.text: Woman welcome to bundle up the corn

parts.note: she refers to a woman
ave is a Latin greeting, hail or welcome

explanation.surface: A woman greets harvest time by tying up the corn.
explanation.walkthrough: AVE is Latin for 'hail', a crossword welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather cut corn stalks into bound bundles is to make them into sheaves.

clue.text: Passed out in a suit

parts.note: cards dealt out to players, all belonging to one suit

explanation.definitionFit: One of the four card suits, dealt out in a game.

clue.text: Good porter gets the wind up

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, an ale

explanation.surface: A fine hotel doorman gets frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: Porter looks like a doorman but is a dark beer; 'gets the wind up' sounds like taking fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong wind is a storm-force blow.

clue.text: Camaraderie desired by aspiring Oxbridge academic

definitions.meaning: a college post at Oxford or Cambridge that a young scholar hopes to win

explanation.definitionFit: Companionship among friends; also a college research post at Oxford or Cambridge.

clue.text: Played slowly or fast by orchestral leader

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word orchestral

explanation.surface: Is the music played slow or fast, decided by the lead violinist?
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' seems the opposite of slow but is the noun: LENT, the period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempo marking for music performed at a slow pace.

clue.text: In Amritsar it's a common habit

indicators.note: In means the letters sit within the words Amritsar it's

explanation.surface: In an Indian city, it's a common form of dress.
explanation.walkthrough: Habit means dress, not custom; Amritsar is a city in Punjab, India.
explanation.definitionFit: Habit can mean clothing; the draped garment is everyday wear for Indian women.

clue.text: I'm in a state after cartoon work

indicators.note: in places the letters of I'm inside the word for state

parts.note: a state is a nation

explanation.surface: Someone is upset after working on cartoons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' sounds like being agitated; really 'in' puts I'M inside a word for state, with 'a' in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Animated cartoons are made by drawing successive frames to give movement.

clue.text: Prize given to a child in care

parts.note: a ward is a child under the protection of a guardian or court

explanation.surface: A trophy goes to a youngster in foster care.
explanation.definitionFit: A prize is something won or bestowed, a synonym.

clue.text: Twin poles in action are getting into gear

indicators.note: in puts the twin pole letters inside the word for action

parts.note: doing is action
N, north, is a pole, and two of them give NN

explanation.surface: Two poles in motion are shifting into gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting into gear' means putting on clothes, not a car shifting gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting into one's gear is putting clothes on.

clue.text: Ken & Roy's involvement in Scotland

indicators.note: involvement suggests the letters are tangled up together in a new order

parts.note: the S of the possessive is kept as a letter here

explanation.surface: Two men named Ken and Roy are involved with Scottish affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involvement' rearranges KEN plus ROYS; the islands lie off northern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: These islands lie off the northern tip of the Scottish mainland, part of the country.
